title: Villarroel transients on 1950s plates correlate with nuclear tests
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Villarroel transients on 1950s plates correlate with nuclear tests, about 1950s at Palomar sky survey plates, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote:

with nuclear. It's 68% more likely to

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a study by an astronomer, Beatriz Villarroel, of the Palomar sky survey, a set of photographic glass plates of the night sky taken in the 1950s. On these plates she looked at "transients", points of light that appear in one picture and are gone in the next, and Michels says her study found they were 68% more likely to show up within 24 hours of a nuclear bomb test. If true, it would hint that something in the sky was reacting to humanity's nuclear tests.
